main_text.l: mari dicuntur? Cassander ille (qui
Coloniae resipuit ante obitum, & indicta sua
cupiens, professioni fidei Pii IV.
pag.218. subscripsit) saltem occasionem dat ex-
plicandi negotium; si tamen id meretur
peculiarem operam, inspicerem obser-
vationes Sacras Josephi Vicecomitis: verum
mon reperiuntur in hisce regioni-
bus: porro unum necessarium est. Ma-
gne vir, Deus te conservet Ecclesiæ suæ
bono, seu splendori potius, ut conserva-
vit hactenus.
Est hic locorum vir
aliqvis excellens, tui æstimantissimus, qui
vocatur Leonardus Marius, is te cupit
salvere plurimum, ut ego, si occasio tu-
lerit, Veronium etiam ac Rigaltium;
qui nec abjuravi scribere: deinceps quoque,
nihil dissimulo, quia gaudio plenus, è literis tuis, Patrone exoptatissime, penitusque optime.
Amstelodami xij Martii,
cIↄ IↄCXLIX.
EPIST. LXVII. Abraham Ecchellensis Johanni Morino mittit capita Epitomes constitutio-num

page.notes: The word "Cassander" begins with a superscript "a" printed above the C, shown here as plain "Ca" in the original. The word "mon" in "verum mon reperiuntur" is printed in bold type, which is a printing irregularity and is kept as printed. The date "cIↄ IↄCXLIX." is an old Roman numeral form for MDCXLIX. The reference "pag.218." is in italic type. The letter-title line ends with the hyphenated word "constitutio-" continued as "num". No catchword, signature or marginal notes appear on this page.
